## Why
Compaction preserves folded event sources as `*.retired` (invariant I1, epic b306); retention is permanent, so tombstones — and the whole per-event commit/tree history — accumulate on the `tickets` branch. This blocks health-lane bug `defensive-buckskin-rhino` (`a453-193b-2864-451b`): the blobless CI checkout pack is ~481 MiB vs a deliberate 100 MiB budget (`verify-identity.yml:47`). A `git gc`/repack does NOT shrink it (proven). The only lever is reducing reachable commit/tree objects on `tickets` history — causally-safe history reclamation, which requires the causal-stability proof this epic owns.

## Operator decision (2026-08-24, in comments)
Stability model = **option 2 (remote-anchored horizon) + stale-clone forced override**, N=30d default; residual loss of a >N-day-drifted clone's divergent work is ACCEPTED.

## Design + proof (full detail in the DESIGN + PROOF comment)
Causal-stability boundary C1–C5: an event is reclaimable iff (C1) folded by a committed SNAPSHOT, (C2) that fold reachable on the sync remote's `tickets` ref ≥ N days, (C3) stale clones (> N days) forced to reset to remote (no reintroduction), (C4) its signature is carried in the SNAPSHOT `authorship_ledger` OR `identity.enforce_since` is re-anchored to grandfather it, (C5) no unfolded state depends on it (I9). Under C1–C5 no still-observable state changes, no signature verification breaks, no resurrection is possible.

**Swap safety for ALL clone states (extends C3):** the ref swap applies a WRITE-FENCE — the sync remote is quiesced and all in-flight pushes are drained before the swap — so no live (<N-day) clone holds unpushed divergent writes at swap time. A <N-day clone reconnecting after the swap rebases/replays its post-baseline (in-horizon) events onto the new baseline (those events are above the horizon and untouched by the collapse of pre-horizon history), losing NO observable work. Only >N-day clones lose divergent local work (the explicitly accepted loss). So the no-lost-observable-work claim covers every clone state, not just >N-day drift.

Measured (origin/tickets): 235,482 commits, 408,295 trees, ZERO blobs blobless; trees ≈95% of bytes; root tree 270 KB × 6,008 flat ticket dirs re-emitted per commit; ~69% of commits are derived enrichment/digest churn; ~14K commits/day.

## Quantified win — insufficient alone
`.retired` files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless ⇒ `.retired` GC alone shrinks it by ~0. The real lever is collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints below the horizon. Max safe win at N=30d ≈ 365–380 MiB; N=7d ≈ 200–215 MiB; reaching ≤100 MiB needs an unsafe <4-day horizon. **So a temporary budget-raise bridge (W3) is unavoidable**, paired with structural fixes (out of scope, `discovered_from` this epic): W1 batch the enrichment/digest write lane; W2 shard the flat ticket dirs to shrink root-tree churn.

## Mechanism (portable, out-of-band; NO CI-provider dependence)
Offline reclamation in a disposable clone (I9b isolation), never on an interactive path or under the store lock:
- **S1** remote-anchored eligibility (horizon computation) — pure git reachability + timestamps.
- **S2** history coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint = compacted as-of-horizon state + carried authorship_ledger; re-anchor `identity.enforce_since` to the baseline. Broadened from `.retired`-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever).
- **S3** stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect (with the write-fence above).
- **S0** ADR: amend §I1 permanent-retention doctrine; prove I1–I9 hold under the horizon with the accepted >N-day loss.

## Risk / rollback
A rewrite changes every commit SHA ⇒ every clone/worktree diverges (non-FF force-update of a shared, auto-pushed, high-write-rate branch); the write-fence + maintenance window bounds in-flight loss to the accepted >N-day case. Rollback: immutable backup ref `refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date>` before the swap; stage on a shadow branch verified by `rebar fsck` + full-log replay + `verify-authorship`; the swap is one revertible ref update; never prune the backup until a green Verify Authorship Identity run + full reconcile.

## Acceptance criteria — THIS design slice (completable now)
- [ ] Causal-stability boundary C1–C5 specified with citations and PROVEN: no still-observable state change, no signature-verification break, no resurrection; covering all clone states incl. <N-day unpushed writes.
- [ ] Pack-shrink quantified vs the 100 MiB budget from measured object composition; shown INSUFFICIENT alone; W3 budget-bridge value + W1/W2 structural follow-ups identified.
- [ ] Safe mechanism (S0–S3), portability (no single CI provider), and risk/rollback DESIGNED.
- [ ] Escalated to a human for approval before any destructive/history-rewriting action.

## Deferred to later child slices (S0–S3 — NOT implemented in this slice; only after approval)
- [ ] S0 ADR: §I1 doctrine amended; I1–I9 proven under horizon+override; accepted >N-day loss stated.
- [ ] S1 eligibility algorithm implemented (remote-reachable ≥ N days; recent excluded; portable).
- [ ] S2 coalescing prototyped on a DISPOSABLE SHADOW CLONE (I9b isolation, never pushed): commit/tree count reduced vs baseline; re-signed baseline; `enforce_since` re-anchored; `rebar fsck` + replay + `verify-authorship` clean ON THE SHADOW BRANCH; two-clone resurrection test.
- [ ] S3 stale-clone override enforced on reconnect.
- [ ] docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved to 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set + W1/W2 filed.

## HARD STOP (this design slice only)
This slice is DESIGN + PROOF only: no history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed, and none of the deferred S0–S3 implementation ACs are done here. All S0–S3 implementation (incl. the S2 shadow-clone prototype) happens in later child slices AFTER human approval, and never mutates origin/tickets or the Gerrit box until the approved staged rollout. Escalated to the orchestrator for human approval before any destructive action.
